summary: The second revision of the BBN schedule for adding core memory to IMPs and TIPs. Retrofits at several sites were completed and removed, and others were rescheduled. It restates the text of RFC 447.

eli5.summary: An updated calendar for the network box memory upgrades, with finished sites crossed off and a few dates moved.

questions: how much memory did a tip have in 1973
subtitle: A dated list of when each ARPANET IMP and TIP would get its extra core memory in early 1973.

tldr.problem: BBN was adding core memory to every IMP and TIP and needed sites to know when their machine would be down for the upgrade.
tldr.mechanism: The note restates the plan from RFC 447, removes the sites already finished, reschedules a few others and lists the remaining dates.
tldr.outcome: It is a short-lived operational schedule, and it replaces RFC 447.

today: This revision of RFC 447 was a dated operational schedule for 1973. Its status is listed as Unknown and the text describes no later use.

sections.title: What Changed in This Revision
sections.content:
This is the second revision of the memory retrofit schedule first given in RFC 447. It makes two kinds of change. The retrofits at Utah, Belvoir, NOAA, USC, Stanford, ISI, Case and CCA are done and are removed. The retrofits at UCSB, ETAC, Aberdeen and Rome are rescheduled.

The rest of the note repeats the revised text of RFC 447.
sections.eli5: Some sites already got their upgrade, so they are crossed off, and a few dates moved.

sections.title: The Memory Retrofit Plan
sections.content:
During the first several months of 1973, BBN retrofits each IMP and TIP with additional core memory. When the program ends, the machines will have these sizes: an IMP (516 or 316) will have 16K words, a TIP will have 28K words, and a TIP with the Magnetic Tape Option will have 32K words.

The larger TIP memory means the TIP must be enlarged to two cabinets. A site that expects trouble with the extra floor space should contact Hawley Rising at BBN.
sections.eli5: Each network box gets a bigger memory. The biggest ones also need a second cabinet, so they need more room on the floor.

sections.title: The Remaining Schedule
sections.content:
The dates were chosen to coincide with each site's usual monthly Preventive Maintenance, to cause the least user inconvenience. The work often needs the machine down longer than normal. Dates are given as month/day.

The remaining list runs from SRI on 3/7, ETAC and FNWC on 3/15, Rome on 3/16, UCLA on 3/19, AMES IMP on 3/21 and GWC on 3/22, through Carnegie on 4/4, SDC on 4/17, Illinois on 4/18 and UCSB on 5/1. Aberdeen is listed as postponed indefinitely. The author promises further RFCs if the schedule needs updating.
sections.eli5: Each site gets a day on the calendar, usually the day its box is already being serviced. One site's day was put off with no new date.

references.text: McKenzie, A., "IMP/TIP Memory Retrofit Schedule", RFC 447.
